hook: Your party invite breaks into eight numbered pieces and hops through Wi-Fi, your internet provider, routers and a message app's server to Juno's tablet. Make one choice at each stop, then see every place a copy now lives.
outcome: Explain that a message is cut into numbered pieces that travel through many devices and are put back in order, and decide which personal details are safe to share online
sources: CSTA K-12 Computer Science Standards, 2026 identifiers E3-SYS-NT-14, E3-SYS-SE-13, E3-SYS-IM-15; 2017 standards 1B-NI-04 and 1B-NI-05: https://csteachers.org/k12standards/
Khan Academy, Computers and the Internet, "The Internet: Packets, routing and reliability": https://www.khanacademy.org/computing/computers-and-internet
FTC Consumer Advice, "Are Public Wi-Fi Networks Safe? What You Need to Know": https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/are-public-wi-fi-networks-safe-what-you-need-know
FTC Consumer Advice, "Kids and Socializing Online": https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/kids-and-socializing-online
Common Sense Education, Digital Citizenship, "Private and Personal Information": https://www.commonsense.org/education/digital-citizenship
